Metabolic DNA as the origin of spontaneously released DNA? A DNA fraction is spontaneously released from living, but not dead or dying, human, other mammalian, avian, amphibian, plant, and prokaryote cells. The spontaneously released DNA fraction has been shown to be (a) present in both actively dividing and nondividing, differentiated cell populations; (b) labile; (c) associated with DNA-dependent RNA or DNA polymerase; (d) associated with an RNA fraction; and to have (e) a lower molecular weight than the typical genetic DNA fraction; and (f) Alu repeat sequences in increased proportions compared to a unique gene in plasma/serum.
